title: Potential dualizing complexes with prime-power coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $T$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; excellent means that its affine coordinate rings are excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use the small etale derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $\Lambda_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}$, the sheaf of units with $u^{\ell^n}=1$, acted on by exponentiation; positive twists are tensor powers, the zeroth twist is $\Lambda_T$, and negative twists are powers of the module dual [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. A dimension function $\delta:|T|\to\mathbf Z$ satisfies $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ at every immediate geometric specialization $y\rightsquigarrow x$ (codimension one after strict localization at $x$). For a point $x$, let $R\Gamma_xK$ be extraordinary restriction to the closed point after restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}$, an object on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-residue-field]; at a geometric point take its geometric fibre, equivalently supported cohomology on the strict henselization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].

A pinned potential dualizing complex for $(T,\delta,\Lambda)$ is $K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ with isomorphisms $p_x:R\Gamma_xK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]$ such that, after geometric restriction, $p_y=p_x(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{y,x}$ for every immediate specialization. The normalized residue map $\operatorname{sp}_{y,x}:R\Gamma_yK\to R\Gamma_xK(1)[2]$ is constructed as follows. In the strict localization at $x$, take the reduced closure $Z$ of $y$ and its normalization $\widetilde Z$ [def-sc-normalization], a strictly henselian trait. On that trait use the tame-inertia residue transition for extraordinary restriction of $K$ to $Z$, divided by the purely inseparable degree $[\kappa(\widetilde x):\kappa(x)]$, which is invertible in $\Lambda$. The trait transition is the map from the generic fibre twisted by $-1$ to the degree-two term of the supported-cohomology model $M_x\to M_y^S\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda[[G]]}(I_G,M_y^S)$: $S$ is wild inertia, $G$ tame inertia, $I_G$ its augmentation ideal; use averaging over $S$ and evaluation on $1-\sigma$ for a tame generator $\sigma$, termwise and totalized for complexes. A morphism of pinned complexes is a derived-category morphism whose induced maps on every $R\Gamma_x$ respect $p_x$.
